text:
Jen: heads up — new rollout to prod (model-serving v2.14) is showing rapid restarts in the inference pods, started ~5m after deploy. Seeing crashloop backoffs on ~30% of replicas.

Ashwin: noticed it too, logs show sidecar health probe failing, but model container seems up. stack traces look like `context deadline exceeded` from the sidecar liveness check.

IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert: prod: model-serving - repeated container restarts (CRITICAL). Paging sam-oncall.

Sam: I'm on it, paging me and confirming I'm scooping the incident. Can someone paste the deployment name?

Miguel: deployment: model-serve-prod-v2, namespace: infra-inference.

Dana: quick check — I see readiness probe failures at a 5s interval for the sidecar. The main container has no OOMs and no stacktraces. Sidecar logs show a short tcp dial timeout to 127.0.0.1:8081 then exits.

Jen: that port is the local health shim (sidecar -> model). Could the startup ordering have changed in the image? We changed preStop hook in this rollout.

Ashwin: yes we added a small init that delays sidecar start until model ready, but timing could cause a race where Kubernetes deems the pod unhealthy during probe cycle.

Sam: immediate mitigation: pause the rollout and scale the deployment down to existing stable replicas. I'm going to pause the k8s rollout now.

DeployBot: `kubectl rollout pause deployment/model-serve-prod-v2 -n infra-inference` executed by Sam (initiated).

Sam: rolling rollout paused. Next step — scale down new RS to 0 to stop churn.

Dana: `kubectl scale deployment/model-serve-prod-v2 --replicas=3 -n infra-inference` (scaling to stable replica count). Doing it now.

Ashwin: copying logs from a failing sidecar:
```
2026-03-15T12:04:17Z WARN healthcheck: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:8081: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T12:04:18Z INFO shutting down sidecar
```
Main container logs show normal readiness/gRPC health ok.

Miguel: customer-facing impact? Support dashboard shows a spike in 503s for inference endpoint over the last 8m. Impacted requests ~14% of total traffic, primarily long-context batch requests.

SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-73. Customers affected: alpha-integration, beta-saas-team (partial). Ticket links: https://support.redwood/in/INC-2026-0315-73

Jen: good catch. We need to revert the preStop/init change in the sidecar image or roll back to previous stable replica set. Thoughts?

Ashwin: fastest is to rollback the deployment to lastRevision. We don't have a hotfix build yet. I'll prepare the rollback command.

Sam: agreed. Trigger rollback and monitor traffic. Also open a feature-flag kill so clients hit the older path if needed.

DeployBot: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-serve-prod-v2 -n infra-inference --to-revision=2` executed by Ashwin.

Dana: rollback started, new pods coming up behind stable RS. Observed reduced restarts within 2 minutes.

Miguel: 503 rate dropped from 14% -> 2% within 4 minutes after rollback. Customer impact now minimal.

Jen: P1 mitigation done. Sam, please confirm on-call handoff and page SRE rotation for postmortem tomorrow.

Sam: I'll stay on for 30m to watch for regressions, then hand off to Dana. Paging @Dana for takeover at 13:00 UTC.

IncidentBot: @Dana you have been assigned the on-call handover for this incident.

Dana: ack. I'll take it. I'll run a quick probe sweep across regions and check autoscaler events.

Ashwin: root cause hypothesis: our init container change introduced a startup ordering window where the sidecar probe runs before the model IPC socket is ready, causing the sidecar to exit and trigger restart loop. Needs an improvement in probe (longer initialDelaySeconds) or guard in sidecar to backoff instead of exit.

Jen: immediate actions: 1) rollback completed (done), 2) toggle feature-flag to route heavy batch traffic away from v2 (Sam did this), 3) create follow-up RFC for probe semantics.

Miguel: I've updated the incident ticket with customer impact timeline and mitigation steps. We should notify the two customers with a short note: "Partial 503s for ~8 minutes, automated rollback applied; please retry requests."

SupportBot: Draft message prepared for customers. Jen, approve?

Jen: approve. Send.

Dana: monitoring: CPU and memory look normal. HPA didn't scale; HPA events show no anomalies. No node drains or cordons observed.

Ashwin: for the postmortem I'll include the reproducible sequence and a short dev test to run before rollout (start sidecar with aggressive probe). Also will add an automated gating check to catch sidecar startup exits in canaries.

Sam: handoff notes for Dana: keep alerting thresholds tightened for next 2 hours, if 5xx rate >3% for 5m, page me.

Dana: noted. I'll run through the kube events and collect `kubectl describe` + `kubectl logs` for the failed pods and attach to INC-2026-0315-73.

Jen: thanks team. We'll schedule a postmortem and action items: revert preStop change in repo, add probe backoff logic in sidecar, add a canary gating job.

Ashwin: ETA for dev fix ~1 day, go/no-go in next deploy after changes.

Sam: closing incident in Slack thread after handoff. We'll follow up in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-0315-73 status: mitigated, assigned to Dana for follow-up and postmortem.

Miguel: leaving log excerpts in the ticket and marking customers notified.

SupportBot: Customer notifications sent.

Dana: taking over — compiling artifacts now, will post postmortem draft in 24h.

Jen: good job everyone, nice quick rollback and coordinated handoff. :bow:
